easy.def: To take something that is given to you.
examples: I accept the gift.
She accepted the prize.
He accepts the cookie.

more.def: To take something that is offered to you.
examples: She accepted the prize with a smile.
Will you accept my invitation to the party?
The cashier accepts coins and bills.

easy.def: The way to get in or use something.
examples: We have access to the library.
There is access to the beach.
Do you have access?

more.def: The ability or right to enter, use or get something.
examples: The students have access to the library.
A path gives access to the beach.
Everyone has access to clean water.

easy.def: Something bad that happens that no one wanted to happen.
examples: I spilled my milk by accident.
There was a car accident on our street.
Dropping the plate was an accident.

more.def: Something that happens by chance and is not planned, often causing harm or damage.
examples: He broke the vase by accident when he bumped the table.
We met by accident at the grocery store.
Wearing a helmet can protect you in a bike accident.
According to Mom, it is time for bed.
According to the map, we turn here.
According to the weather report, it will rain.

more.def: As said by someone or shown by something.
examples: According to the map, we turn left here.
According to my teacher, the test is Friday.
The park is closed, according to the sign.

easy.def: A story that tells what happened.
examples: She gave an account of the trip.
The account was short.
He wrote an account of the storm.

more.def: A report or story that tells what happened.
examples: She gave an account of the trip to her class.
He wrote an account of the storm for the newspaper.
The explorer's account was published.
I have an account at the bank.
Mom put money in my account.
The account has ten dollars.

more.def: An arrangement with a bank where your money is kept safe.
examples: She opened a savings account with her birthday money.
Dad checks his account online.
I put five dollars in my account.

easy.def: To do something you worked hard for.
examples: You can achieve your goal if you keep trying.
He achieved his goal of riding a bike.
I want to achieve a high score.

more.def: To succeed in doing something through effort or skill.
examples: She achieved her dream of swimming across the lake.
The class achieved its goal of reading one hundred books.
You can achieve a lot when you practice every day.

easy.def: From one side to the other.
examples: Walk across the street.
A bridge goes across the river.
We swam across the lake.

more.def: From one side of something to the other.
examples: A bridge stretches across the river.
She ran across the field.
He drew a line across the page.

easy.def: From one side to the other.
examples: The lake is a mile across.
The kids ran across and waved.
We got across by boat.

more.def: To or on the other side.
examples: The lake is a mile across at its widest point.
The kids ran across and waved from the far side.
The river is wide, but we can get across by boat.

easy.def: To play a part in a play.
examples: I act in the school play.
She acted like a dragon.
We act out the story.

more.def: To play a character in a play, movie or show.
examples: She will act the part of a queen in the school play.
Many actors begin to act when they are very young.
The twins acted out a funny scene for the class.

easy.def: To behave in a certain way.
examples: My baby brother acts shy.
The dog acts scared in a storm.
Try to act calm.

more.def: To behave in a particular way.
examples: My little brother acts shy around strangers.
The puppy acted scared when it heard the thunder.
Try to act calmly if a bee flies near you.
Sharing your snack is a kind act.
Saving the cat was a brave act.
Cleaning the park was a good act.

more.def: A single thing that a person does.
examples: Picking up litter at the beach was a simple act that helped the birds.
The firefighter's brave act saved the little dog.
An act of kindness can make someone's whole day better.
Cleaning up was a kind action.
His quick action helped.
She took action and called for help.
Her kind action made me smile.
A quick action saved the toy from falling.
He took action and called for help.

easy.def: A person who plays a part in a play or movie.
examples: The actor played a king.
My uncle is an actor.
The actors bowed.

more.def: A person who plays a character in a play, movie or show.
examples: The actor played the part of a pirate.
My aunt is a famous actor.
The actors bowed to the cheering crowd.
I am actually seven.
It actually works.
She actually won.

more.def: Used to say what is true, especially when it is surprising.
examples: The tomato is actually a fruit, not a vegetable.
I thought the test would be hard, but it was actually easy.
He actually caught the ball with one hand.
